bull.b: Consistent, large free cash flow (TTM ~$13.4B and H1 adjusted automotive FCF supporting $2.8B buybacks) provides durable funding for capex, EV transition and buybacks. This cash generation improves strategic optionality and cushions cyclical revenue swings over the medium term.

bull.t: Truck leadership & North America margin recovery
bull.b: Dominant full-size pickup share (>42%) plus North America adj EBIT margin back in the 8%–10% target indicate strong product competitiveness and pricing power. This stable truck franchise drives durable cash and profit generation, insulating overall results from weaker segments.

A 20-year extension of the SAIC‑GM JV secures long-term China market access and localized NEV development. The commitment to launch ≥30 new energy models through 2030 preserves scale, local R&D and manufacturing advantages vital for EV competitiveness and international technology transfer.

bear.b: Debt-to-equity around 2x is high for a cyclical OEM and limits balance-sheet flexibility. Elevated leverage raises refinancing and interest risks, constrains ability to fund sustained EV investment or absorb demand shocks, and reduces buffer during industry downturns.

A sharp decline in gross and operating margins substantially lowers resilience to volume or cost setbacks. Persistently compressed margins reduce ROE and free cash conversion, making it harder to self-fund EV launches, warranty repairs and onshoring without relying on external financing or slower buybacks.

bear.t: Large EV restructuring charges & cash impact
bear.b: Substantial, ongoing EV-related writedowns and cash costs materially strain resources and reflect execution risk. Large charges and lower EV volumes increase uncertainty around reaching sustainable EV margins and may require additional restructuring or investment to achieve profitable scale over the medium term.
